references.name: Middletown
William Nordhaus
references.connection:
Calculated the 800-fold improvement in lighting
        purchasing power; estimated health capital doubles
        measured growth 1900–1950

references.name: Paul David
references.connection:
Dynamo analogy — 40-year lag between Edison
        and electrification of manufacturing — explains
        delayed productivity payoffs from GPTs

references.name: Alex Field
references.connection:
Documented the 1930s as the most productive decade
        in U.S. economic history; calculated $1B telegraph
        social benefit (7% of 1890 GDP)

references.name: Piketty & Saez
references.connection:
Income distribution data identifying the three
        eras: compression (1917–48), golden age (1948–72),
        Great Divergence (1972–present)

references.name: Claudia Goldin
David Cutler & Grant Miller
references.connection:
Clean water explains 50% of overall mortality
        reduction and 75% of infant mortality decline
        1900–1936

references.name: McKinlay & McKinlay
references.connection:
Medical care contributes at most 3.5% of
        mortality decline since 1900; most decline
        preceded medical interventions

references.name: Abraham Flexner
references.connection:
1910 Flexner Report that devastated for-profit
        medical schools and transformed American medical
        education

references.name: James Heckman
David Autor et al.
references.connection:
China imports account for ~25% of manufacturing
        employment decline 1990–2007; automation destroying
        routine middle-skill jobs

references.name: Charles Murray
references.connection:
"Fishtown" data: two-parent family collapse in
        bottom third of white population, 95% (1960)
        to 34% (2010)

references.name: Ruth Schwartz Cowan
references.connection:
Appliances paradox: consumer technology didn't
        reduce total home production hours because rising
        standards absorbed the time savings

references.name: Upton Sinclair, The Jungle
references.connection:
Intended as labor expose; became food safety
        catalyst; directly led to the Pure Food and
        Drug Act of 1906
